lede: The story of Christmas in McKinney begins in 1848, when the new county seat of Collin County was chosen, and today it centers on the historic downtown square, where Home for the Holidays lights the community tree on Thanksgiving weekend and Santa on the Square sets up Santa's Little Workshop. The Heard Natural Science Museum, open since October 1, 1967, adds Holidays at the Heard, part of 6 McKinney events this season.
sections: Named for Collin McKinney, county seat since 1848

McKinney is named for Collin McKinney, a signer of the Texas Declaration of Independence. The First Legislature of Texas called for a new county seat site on January 12, 1848, and McKinney was chosen by a vote of ten to one. William Davis donated 120 acres for the townsite on March 24, 1849. The town had 35 people in 1848 and 4,714 in 1912, and the Handbook of Texas lists 202,690 by 2021. Before McKinney, the county seat of Collin County was Buckner, which served for the first two years.
Home for the Holidays and Santa on the Square

Home for the Holidays is McKinney's Thanksgiving weekend celebration across the 14 block historic downtown, Friday, November 27, through Sunday, November 29, 2026, free, around 111 North Tennessee Street. It includes the Community Tree Lighting, live entertainment, Santa visits, costumed characters and children's activities. Santa on the Square follows with Santa's Little Workshop in the little houses at Virginia and Kentucky Streets, in front of the McKinney Performing Arts Center, on December 3 to 6, 10 to 13 and 17 to 20. A Classic Visit is $39 per family for about five minutes, booked in advance.
Rails, an interurban and a night at the Heard

The Houston and Texas Central Railway reached McKinney in 1872 and the Missouri, Kansas and Texas Railroad in 1881. From 1908 to 1948 the Texas Electric Railroad linked McKinney with Denison, Dallas and Waco. Another McKinney landmark, the Heard Natural Science Museum and Wildlife Sanctuary, grew from the Bessie Heard Foundation formed in 1964 and opened on October 1, 1967. Its Holidays at the Heard puts lights and Santa on a nature trail from 6 to 9 pm on December 11, 12 and 13, 2026, at 1 Nature Place, with tickets of $17 for adults and $14 for children 3 to 12.

faq: How did McKinney get its name?

McKinney is named for Collin McKinney, a signer of the Texas Declaration of Independence. The First Legislature of Texas called for a new county seat site on January 12, 1848, and McKinney was chosen by a vote of ten to one. William Davis donated 120 acres for the townsite on March 24, 1849.
When is the McKinney tree lighting?

The Community Tree Lighting is part of Home for the Holidays in Historic Downtown McKinney, which runs Friday, November 27, through Sunday, November 29, 2026, around 111 North Tennessee Street. The event is free. The festival also has live entertainment, Santa visits, costumed characters and children's activities across the historic square.
Where can kids meet Santa in McKinney?

Santa on the Square sets up Santa's Little Workshop at Virginia and Kentucky Streets, in front of the McKinney Performing Arts Center, on December 3 to 6, 10 to 13 and 17 to 20, 2026. A Classic Visit is a $39 family reservation, and visits are indoors. Santa also appears at Holidays at the Heard from 6:30 to 8 pm.
Did a train ever run through McKinney?

Yes. The Houston and Texas Central Railway reached McKinney in 1872, and the Missouri, Kansas and Texas Railroad reached it in 1881. The Texas Electric Railroad, an interurban line running from Denison to Dallas and Waco, served McKinney from 1908 to 1948, according to the Handbook of Texas.
How did the Heard Museum start?

Bessie Heard, who lived from 1886 to 1988, came up with the project at age 80. The Bessie Heard Foundation formed in 1964, construction began in 1966 and the museum opened on October 1, 1967. A 50 acre wetlands was finished in 1992, and the sanctuary now covers 289 acres.
